title: Training Job Stuck Pending for Six Hours
intro: The nightly retraining job hasn't started. Its pod has been Pending since midnight. The GPU cluster has 16 GPUs — surely enough for a job that needs 2?

steps.prompt: Check why the training pod can't be scheduled.
steps.fake_output:
Events:
  Warning  FailedScheduling  default-scheduler  0/6 nodes are available: 2 Insufficient nvidia.com/gpu, 4 node(s) didn't match Pod's node affinity/selector.
steps.hint: The scheduler's event says exactly what's missing.

steps.prompt: Both GPU nodes are out of GPUs. See what's holding the GPUs on gpu-node-1.
expected_commands: kubectl describe node gpu-node-1 | grep -A10 "Non-terminated Pods"
steps.fake_output:
Non-terminated Pods:
  ml-team  jupyter-alice-0      nvidia.com/gpu: 4   Age: 23d
  ml-team  jupyter-bob-0        nvidia.com/gpu: 2   Age: 41d
  ml-team  hpo-trial-17         nvidia.com/gpu: 2   Age: 9d
steps.hint: Look at the age of each GPU-holding pod.

steps.prompt: Check whether those notebook pods are actually using their GPUs right now.
steps.fake_output:
utilization.gpu [%], memory.used [MiB]
0 %, 0 MiB
0 %, 0 MiB
0 %, 0 MiB
0 %, 0 MiB
steps.hint: 0% utilization and no memory used means idle.

steps.prompt: hpo-trial-17 is a hyperparameter-search trial from 9 days ago. Check its job status.
steps.hint: Is it making progress, or hung?

steps.prompt: After confirming with its owner that the trial is hung, delete it to free its GPUs.
steps.hint: Always confirm with the owner before deleting someone else's workload.

resolution: The cluster had plenty of GPUs, but they were hoarded: idle Jupyter notebooks holding 6 GPUs for weeks at 0% utilization, and a hung hyperparameter trial holding 2 more. In Kubernetes a GPU requested by a pod is exclusively reserved whether used or not, so the scheduler correctly saw zero available. Freeing the hung trial let tonight's job run. Durable fixes: auto-cull idle notebooks (JupyterHub's idle culler), set activeDeadlineSeconds on training jobs so hung ones terminate themselves, use ResourceQuotas to cap GPUs per team, use priority classes so scheduled production retraining can preempt experimentation, and put GPU utilization on a dashboard — idle-but-allocated GPUs are one of the biggest sources of wasted ML infrastructure spend.
